item.title: AI Chatbot or Live Chat for Solar Warranty Enquiries?
item.description:
A customer messages your website at 9pm on a Sunday: “My inverter is showing a red light and the app says zero generation. Is this covered?” What happens next decides whether you keep a happy customer or pick up a one-star review and a Fair Trading complaint.

Most solar businesses I talk to have no plan for that message. It lands in a generic inbox, someone sees it Monday afternoon, and by then the customer has already rung the manufacturer, been told to “contact your installer”, and decided you’re dodging them.

item.title: Will This Solar Brand Still Exist When the Warranty Claim Comes In?
item.description: Every budget panel on the market carries a 25-year performance warranty. That number is printed on the datasheet, it goes on the quote, and the customer nods along like it means something. The question I learned to ask a long time ago, after watching the same movie play out more than once, is simpler and harder: who is actually going to be standing behind that piece of paper in year 10?

item.title: How to Vet a Solar Brand's Warranty Process Before You Commit
item.description: Every brand rep who walks through your door will hand you a warranty document. Twenty-five years on the panels, ten or twelve on the inverter, a glossy line about peace of mind. That document is the easy part. It is also close to worthless as a buying signal, because it tells you what the brand promises, not what the brand actually does when a unit dies in year three and your customer is ringing you every second day.
